newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - Halliburton trades up.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - Halliburton trades up.

text.p: Halliburton Co traded slightly higher in after hours trading Monday, up 1/4 to 80-7/8, after announcing it would acquire NUMAR Corp in a stock swap valued at $360 million, or about $39.62 per Numar share.
The gain did not offset losses on the day however. Halliburton had closed down 1-3/8, at 80-5/8.
NUMAR did not trade at all, traders said, remaining halted at 20-3/4 despite a bid of 30.
"There's a couple of buyers that have popped up," a dealer said, "but we haven't got a sale yet."
Halliburton, an energy services company, said it expected the acquisition to be tax-free, and "modestly dilutive to near-term earnings per share."
In addition, the company said it did not expect the deal to be dilutive to 1998 earnings.

In other news, LSI Logic Corp stock edged down by 1/4 to 33-3/4 in after hours trading after a Montgomery Securities report suggested the company's revenue growth could be slimmer than expected in the third quarter.
The circuit and microprocessor maker's shares plunged by 5-1/8, or 13 percent, during regular hours trading. The stock was the second most active on the Big Board.
Other stocks traded in line with closing prices, dealers said.
"There's nothing major. I'm not seeing anything trading more than 1/8 or 1/4 off the close," a dealer said.
Regular hours trading, by contrast, saw the Dow Jones industrial average rise 61 points, hitting a record close of 7,539; the Nasdaq index, meanwhile, lost 10 points, closing at 1,402.
The New York Stock Exchange said session one volume fell to 8,200 from Monday's 230,000, while session two volume dropped to 260,000 from Monday's 3,888,360.
